mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure that the S&P 500 anticipates by adjusting downward in 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following such CPI spikes, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in employment (PAYEMS) of more than 20,000 jobs in a month coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no correlation with PAYEMS monthly change (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and home sales (HOUST) simultaneously exceed their prior month's levels by at least 2%, it signals robust demand across sectors, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: dual industrial and housing demand expansion
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the mean of the prior 30 such dual-expansion periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month suggests supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such contractions are not statistically lower than during expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that raises expected equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns during such periods are not higher than the average of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.00%), the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be positive due to lower discount rates applied to future earnings.
failure_condition: Over 10 such easing regimes, average 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (retail sales) unexpectedly declines by more than 10% in a month, it reflects weak consumer demand and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns after such drops are not significantly lower than baseline (p > 0.05).
